road.title: The Road
road.author: Cormac McCarthy
road.why: A father and son walk through a burned-out America in spare, haunting prose; readers call it devastating and unforgettable.

piranesi.title: Piranesi
piranesi.author: Susanna Clarke
piranesi.why: A man lives alone in an endless house of statues and tides, and slowly uncovers its secret; short, strange and beautifully written.

project hail mary.title: Project Hail Mary
project hail mary.author: Andy Weir
project hail mary.why: A lone astronaut wakes up with amnesia on a mission to save Earth; science-driven, funny and impossible to put down.

stand.title: The Stand
stand.author: Stephen King
stand.why: A plague wipes out most of humanity and survivors gather around good or evil figures; a huge, gripping apocalyptic saga.

east of eden.title: East of Eden
east of eden.author: John Steinbeck
east of eden.why: Two California families echo the Cain and Abel story across generations; readers praise its big themes about good, evil and choice.

secret history.title: The Secret History
secret history.author: Donna Tartt
secret history.why: A group of classics students at an elite college drift into murder; immersive, twisty and addictive for fans of dark academia.

little life.title: A Little Life
little life.author: Hanya Yanagihara
little life.why: Four friends in New York, one carrying terrible trauma; a devastating, long read readers say they cried through, with heavy content warnings.

stoner.title: Stoner
stoner.author: John Williams
stoner.why: The quiet life of an ordinary university professor, told with simple, precise prose that moves readers more than they expect.

rebecca.title: Rebecca
rebecca.author: Daphne du Maurier
rebecca.why: A young bride is haunted by her husband's dead first wife at his grand estate; gothic, gripping and famous for its opening lines.

demon copperhead.title: Demon Copperhead
demon copperhead.author: Barbara Kingsolver
demon copperhead.why: David Copperfield retold in Appalachia, following a poor orphan through foster care and addiction; readers call it powerful and heartbreaking.

never let me go.title: Never Let Me Go
never let me go.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
never let me go.why: Students at a strange boarding school slowly learn what their lives are for; quiet, sad and impossible to forget.

blood meridian.title: Blood Meridian
blood meridian.author: Cormac McCarthy
blood meridian.why: A teenage runaway joins a band of scalp hunters in the 1850s borderlands; brutal, poetic and widely called a masterpiece.

educated.title: Educated
educated.author: Tara Westover
educated.why: The author grows up in a survivalist family with no schooling and ends up at Cambridge; readers find it gripping and devastating.

night.title: Night
night.author: Elie Wiesel
night.why: A short first-hand account of a teenager's time in Nazi concentration camps; readers call it essential and crushing.

parable of the sower.title: Parable of the Sower
parable of the sower.author: Octavia E. Butler
parable of the sower.why: A young woman survives a collapsing California and founds a new belief system; chillingly relevant dystopia that readers rate highly.

lonesome dove.title: Lonesome Dove
lonesome dove.author: Larry McMurtry
lonesome dove.why: Two retired Texas Rangers drive cattle to Montana; a sprawling, character-rich western often named among the best American novels.

sparrow.title: The Sparrow
sparrow.author: Mary Doria Russell
sparrow.why: Jesuit missionaries make first contact with aliens and one man returns broken; readers say it is moving and haunting.

james.title: James
james.author: Percival L. Everett
james.why: Huckleberry Finn retold from the point of view of Jim, the enslaved man; readers praise its wit, voice and power.

beloved.title: Beloved
beloved.author: Toni Morrison
beloved.why: Readers mostly say it was too hard to get through, and few recommend it in these comments.

goldfinch.title: The Goldfinch
goldfinch.author: Donna Tartt
goldfinch.why: A boy survives a bombing and keeps a stolen painting that shapes his life; long, absorbing and well liked by many readers.

lolita.title: Lolita
lolita.author: Vladimir Nabokov
lolita.why: An unreliable narrator tells his own disturbing story in dazzling prose; admired for the writing, though some find it hard going.

women.title: The Women
women.author: Kristin Hannah
women.why: A young nurse goes to Vietnam and struggles to come home; readers find it moving and easy to read.

book of the new sun.title: Book of the New Sun
book of the new sun.author: Gene Wolfe
book of the new sun.why: A torturer exiled from his guild travels a far-future Earth in a puzzling, richly written tale; hard, but readers call it a masterpiece.

frankenstein.title: Frankenstein
frankenstein.author: Mary Shelley
frankenstein.why: A scientist creates life and then rejects it; the founding science fiction novel, still praised for its moral questions.

count of monte cristo.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
count of monte cristo.author: Alexandre Dumas
count of monte cristo.why: A wrongly imprisoned sailor escapes and plots elaborate revenge; a long but thrilling classic that readers say flies by.

dark matter.title: Dark Matter
dark matter.author: Blake Crouch
dark matter.why: A physicist is kidnapped into a world where his life went differently; a quick, fun sci-fi thriller.

blindsight.title: Blindsight
blindsight.author: Peter Watts
blindsight.why: A crew meets an alien that may be smarter than they are without being conscious; hard sci-fi that readers find brilliant and chilling.

left hand of darkness.title: The Left Hand of Darkness
left hand of darkness.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
left hand of darkness.why: An envoy visits a planet whose people have no fixed gender; readers value its ideas and humane storytelling.

house of leaves.title: House of Leaves
house of leaves.author: Mark Z. Danielewski
house of leaves.why: A house is bigger inside than out, told through footnotes and odd layouts; hard to put down and hard to forget.

ulysses.title: Ulysses
ulysses.author: James Joyce
ulysses.why: One day in Dublin told in shifting experimental styles; very demanding, but readers enjoy it as funny and rewarding.

circe.title: Circe
circe.author: Madeline Miller
circe.why: The witch from the Odyssey tells her own story; lyrical and absorbing myth retelling that readers love.

bunny.title: Bunny
bunny.author: Mona Awad
bunny.why: A lonely writing student is drawn into a clique of women with a bizarre ritual; weird, funny and unsettling.

dune.title: Dune
dune.author: Frank Herbert
dune.why: A noble family fights for control of a desert planet and its spice; the benchmark for epic science fiction.

poisonwood bible.title: The Poisonwood Bible
poisonwood bible.author: Barbara Kingsolver
poisonwood bible.why: An American missionary family goes to the Congo and falls apart, told by wife and daughters; readers find it well written and powerful.

hyperion.title: Hyperion
hyperion.author: Dan Simmons
hyperion.why: Seven pilgrims tell their stories on the way to a deadly shrine; a Canterbury Tales in space that readers rank among the best.

fine balance.title: A Fine Balance
fine balance.author: Rohinton Mistry
fine balance.why: Four strangers share a flat in 1970s India as politics crush their hopes; readers say it hurts and stays with them for weeks.

pillars of the earth.title: The Pillars of the Earth
pillars of the earth.author: Ken Follett
pillars of the earth.why: Rival builders, nobles and monks struggle over a cathedral in medieval England; a long, gripping page-turner.

annihilation.title: Annihilation
annihilation.author: Jeff VanderMeer
annihilation.why: An expedition enters a strange, shifting zone where nature behaves wrongly; short, eerie and often recommended for fans of weird fiction.

flowers for algernon.title: Flowers for Algernon
flowers for algernon.author: Daniel Keyes
flowers for algernon.why: A man with a learning disability becomes a genius through an experiment; told in diary form, it stays with readers for years.

nightingale.title: The Nightingale
nightingale.author: Kristin Hannah
nightingale.why: Two sisters take different paths in occupied France in World War II; readers say it left them sobbing.

children of time.title: Children of Time
children of time.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
children of time.why: Humanity's last ship meets a world where spiders evolve intelligence; readers rave about its big ideas and inventive aliens.

dungeon crawler carl.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl
dungeon crawler carl.author: Matt Dinniman
dungeon crawler carl.why: Aliens turn Earth into a deadly game show and a man and his cat fight for survival; darkly funny and addictive.

born a crime.title: Born a Crime
born a crime.author: Trevor Noah
born a crime.why: The comedian's childhood in apartheid South Africa as a mixed-race child; readers laugh and cry in equal measure.

kindred.title: Kindred
kindred.author: Octavia E. Butler
kindred.why: A modern Black woman is pulled back in time to a slave plantation; gripping, painful and often called her best book.

geek love.title: Geek Love
geek love.author: Katherine Dunn
geek love.why: A carnival family breeds its own freak-show children; grotesque, inventive and wildly strange for readers who like shocking fiction.

station eleven.title: Station Eleven
station eleven.author: Emily St. John Mandel
station eleven.why: After a flu ends civilization, a travelling theatre troupe keeps art alive; beautifully written and a favourite for quiet apocalypse stories.

endurance.title: Endurance
endurance.author: Alfred Lansing
endurance.why: The true story of Shackleton's ship trapped in Antarctic ice and his crew's survival; readers find it gripping and inspiring.

anathem.title: Anathem
anathem.author: Neal Stephenson
anathem.why: Monks living apart from the world are drawn into a crisis that changes it; dense and slow to start but loved for its ideas.

midnight library.title: The Midnight Library
midnight library.author: Matt Haig
midnight library.why: A woman gets to try lives she might have lived; comforting and quick to read, though a few readers found it shallow.

pachinko.title: Pachinko
pachinko.author: Min Jin Lee
pachinko.why: Four generations of a Korean family in Japan face prejudice and hardship; readers call it raw, real and moving.

into thin air.title: Into Thin Air
into thin air.author: Jon Krakauer
into thin air.why: The author's first-hand account of the deadly 1996 Everest disaster; readers say they could not stop reading.

bell jar.title: The Bell Jar
bell jar.author: Sylvia Plath
bell jar.why: A young woman slides into depression in 1950s New York; readers relate strongly and say it stays with them.

homegoing.title: Homegoing
homegoing.author: Yaa Gyasi
homegoing.why: Two Ghanaian half-sisters and their descendants across 300 years; each chapter follows one generation, and readers find it powerful.

remains of the day.title: The Remains of the Day
remains of the day.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
remains of the day.why: An English butler looks back on a life of duty and missed chances; subtle and quietly devastating.

shogun.title: Shōgun
shogun.author: James Clavell
shogun.why: An English pilot is stranded in feudal Japan and caught in a power struggle; a long, immersive adventure.

lord of the rings.title: The Lord of the Rings
lord of the rings.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
lord of the rings.why: A hobbit sets out to destroy a ring of power; the founding epic of modern fantasy that readers return to again and again.

blindness.title: Blindness
blindness.author: José Saramago
blindness.why: A sudden epidemic of blindness breaks down society; unusual punctuation-free prose and a harrowing story readers praise.

martian.title: The Martian
martian.author: Andy Weir
martian.why: An astronaut stranded on Mars science his way to survival; funny, clever and a quick read.

grapes of wrath.title: The Grapes of Wrath
grapes of wrath.author: John Steinbeck
grapes of wrath.why: A farming family flees the Dust Bowl for California; a powerful picture of poverty and resilience.

devils.title: The Devils
devils.author: Joe Abercrombie
devils.why: Abercrombie's demon-summoning fantasy comedy with bloody action; readers enjoy it so far and plan to read more of his work.

infinite jest.title: Infinite Jest
infinite jest.author: David Foster Wallace
infinite jest.why: A huge, footnoted novel about addiction, tennis and entertainment; very demanding but readers say it rewards the effort.

overstory.title: The Overstory
overstory.author: Richard Powers
overstory.why: Nine people are drawn together by trees and the fight to save forests; ambitious, moving and eye-opening.

slaughterhouse five.title: Slaughterhouse-Five
slaughterhouse five.author: Kurt Vonnegut
slaughterhouse five.why: A soldier becomes unstuck in time after surviving the Dresden bombing; short, funny and sad antiwar classic.

middlemarch.title: Middlemarch
middlemarch.author: George Eliot
middlemarch.why: A study of marriages, ambition and reform in a provincial English town; long and rich, often called the greatest English novel.

in cold blood.title: In Cold Blood
in cold blood.author: Truman Capote
in cold blood.why: A reconstruction of the 1959 murder of a Kansas family and the killers' fate; gripping true crime that reads like a novel.

lamb.title: Lamb
lamb.author: Christopher Moore
lamb.why: The missing years of Jesus told by his best friend Biff; irreverent, hilarious and re-read yearly by fans.

all fours.title: All Fours
all fours.author: Miranda July
all fours.why: A middle-aged artist upends her life on a trip that stops in a motel; funny, odd and hard to predict.

book thief.title: The Book Thief
book thief.author: Markus Zusak
book thief.why: A girl steals books in Nazi Germany while Death narrates; readers love its voice and find it moving.

watership down.title: Watership Down
watership down.author: Richard Adams
watership down.why: Rabbits flee their doomed warren and search for a new home; much more gripping and moving than it sounds.

seveneves.title: Seveneves
seveneves.author: Neal Stephenson
seveneves.why: The moon explodes and humanity races to survive in space; technical and long, but readers like its big ideas.

mans search for meaning.title: Man's Search for Meaning
mans search for meaning.author: Viktor E. Frankl
mans search for meaning.why: A psychiatrist describes surviving Nazi camps and what kept people going; short, humane and widely recommended for finding meaning in suffering.

red rising.title: Red Rising
red rising.author: Pierce Brown
red rising.why: A miner on Mars infiltrates the ruling caste to overthrow it; fast and violent, popular with fans of The Hunger Games and epic fantasy.

my friends.title: My Friends
my friends.author: Fredrik Backman
my friends.why: Backman's novel about friendship and a painting that connects four teenagers; fans who read it praise its warmth and quotable lines.

hitchhikers guide to the galaxy.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
hitchhikers guide to the galaxy.author: Douglas Adams
hitchhikers guide to the galaxy.why: An ordinary man is whisked off Earth moments before it is demolished; absurd, quotable comic science fiction readers love from childhood.

night circus.title: The Night Circus
night circus.author: Erin Morgenstern
night circus.why: Two young magicians are bound in a competition inside a mysterious travelling circus; dreamy and romantic, loved for its imagery.

moby dick.title: Moby-Dick
moby dick.author: Herman Melville
moby dick.why: Captain Ahab hunts the white whale; long and digressive but readers find it funny and sublime.

name of the wind.title: The Name of the Wind
name of the wind.author: Patrick Rothfuss
name of the wind.why: A gifted orphan grows into a legendary wizard, telling his own story; lyrical and absorbing, a fan favourite.

name of the rose.title: The Name of the Rose
name of the rose.author: Umberto Eco
name of the rose.why: A monk investigates murders in a medieval abbey; a learned detective story that readers find rewarding.

one hundred years of solitude.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
one hundred years of solitude.author: Gabriel García Márquez
one hundred years of solitude.why: Seven generations of a family in a Colombian village, full of magic and fate; the classic of magical realism.

shadow of the wind.title: The Shadow of the Wind
shadow of the wind.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
shadow of the wind.why: A boy finds a forgotten book in a Barcelona library of lost books and uncovers its author's mystery; gothic and bookish.

north woods.title: North Woods
north woods.author: Daniel Mason
north woods.why: Centuries of people who live in one New England house and the woods around it; beautifully written and varied.

crime and punishment.title: Crime and Punishment
crime and punishment.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
crime and punishment.why: A poor student commits murder and is consumed by guilt; psychological and intense, it leaves readers in a deep state.

god of small things.title: The God of Small Things
god of small things.author: Arundhati Roy
god of small things.why: Twins in Kerala grow up under the weight of a family tragedy; fascinating and poetic, though not an easy read.

pale fire.title: Pale Fire
pale fire.author: Vladimir Nabokov
pale fire.why: A poem and a madly unreliable commentary on it; a tricky, brilliant puzzle for readers who like playing with form.

glass castle.title: The Glass Castle
glass castle.author: Jeannette Walls
glass castle.why: The author grows up with brilliant but irresponsible parents who drag the family through poverty; compelling and easy to read.

swan song.title: Swan Song
swan song.author: Robert R. McCammon
swan song.why: Survivors of nuclear war fight over what remains of America and its soul; a huge post-apocalyptic story recommended after The Stand.

way of kings.title: The Way of Kings
way of kings.author: Brandon Sanderson
way of kings.why: Warriors, scholars and slaves are drawn into an ancient war on a storm-swept world; Sanderson's huge opening to a vast series.

perfume.title: Perfume
perfume.author: Patrick Süskind
perfume.why: A man with a perfect sense of smell turns to murder to create the ultimate scent; strange, vivid and haunting.

fifth season.title: The Fifth Season
fifth season.author: N. K. Jemisin
fifth season.why: People who can control the earth live in an apocalypse-prone world; inventive and gripping, a Hugo winner.

neuromancer.title: Neuromancer
neuromancer.author: William Gibson
neuromancer.why: A washed-up hacker is hired for one last job in cyberspace; the novel that invented cyberpunk, dense but influential.

doomsday book.title: Doomsday book
doomsday book.author: Connie Willis
doomsday book.why: A historian time-travels to medieval England just as the plague hits; readers say it will break your heart.

haunting of hill house.title: The Haunting of Hill House
haunting of hill house.author: Shirley Jackson
haunting of hill house.why: Four people spend a summer in a haunted mansion with a fragile guest; a masterclass in subtle, creeping dread.

metamorphosis.title: Metamorphosis
metamorphosis.author: Franz Kafka
metamorphosis.why: A man wakes up as a giant insect and his family turns away; very short, strange and widely read.

brave new world.title: Brave New World
brave new world.author: Aldous Huxley
brave new world.why: A future society engineered for happiness and control; a classic dystopia readers still find relevant.

im glad my mom died.title: I'm Glad My Mom Died
im glad my mom died.author: Jennette McCurdy
im glad my mom died.why: The former child actress writes frankly about her controlling mother and her own illness; readers find it raw and darkly funny.

gravitys rainbow.title: Gravity's Rainbow
gravitys rainbow.author: Thomas Pynchon
gravitys rainbow.why: A sprawling, bizarre novel set around V-2 rockets in World War II; famous as one of the hardest books to read.

dracula.title: Dracula
dracula.author: Bram Stoker
dracula.why: Told through letters and diaries, a band of friends hunts the vampire count; surprisingly a page turner.

siddhartha.title: Siddhartha
siddhartha.author: Hermann Hesse
siddhartha.why: A young man in ancient India searches for spiritual understanding; short and lyrical, loved by many and a little preachy to some.

library at mount char.title: The Library at Mount Char
library at mount char.author: Scott Hawkins
library at mount char.why: A group of people raised by a godlike figure are drawn into a struggle for his library; violent, strange and darkly funny.

to kill a mockingbird.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
to kill a mockingbird.author: Harper Lee
to kill a mockingbird.why: A girl in Alabama watches her lawyer father defend a Black man; a warm, moving classic about justice.

will of the many.title: The Will of the Many
will of the many.author: James Islington
will of the many.why: An orphan enters an elite Roman-style academy where the powerful drain others' will; readers call it a gripping start to a series.

shes come undone.title: She's Come Undone
shes come undone.author: Wally Lamb
shes come undone.why: A troubled young woman recounts her difficult life with humour and pain; a popular emotional read.

terror.title: The Terror
terror.author: Dan Simmons
terror.why: Two ships are trapped in Arctic ice in 1845 and something hunts the crew; fiction based on a true expedition that readers cannot put down.

wuthering heights.title: Wuthering Heights
wuthering heights.author: Emily Brontë
wuthering heights.why: An obsessive love between Heathcliff and Cathy destroys two families on the Yorkshire moors; stormy and passionate.

braiding sweetgrass.title: Braiding Sweetgrass
braiding sweetgrass.author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
braiding sweetgrass.why: A botanist and Potawatomi writer joins plant science with indigenous wisdom; readers love it, especially as an audiobook.

hobbit.title: The Hobbit
hobbit.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
hobbit.why: A comfort-loving hobbit is swept into a quest with dwarves to win back treasure from a dragon; a warm, easy adventure.

replay.title: Replay
replay.author: Ken Grimwood
replay.why: A man dies at 43 and wakes up as his 18-year-old self, again and again; an emotional time-loop story.

devil in the white city.title: The Devil in the White City
devil in the white city.author: Erik Larson
devil in the white city.why: The 1893 Chicago World's Fair is told alongside a serial killer working nearby; narrative history that reads like a thriller.

great alone.title: The Great Alone
great alone.author: Kristin Hannah
great alone.why: A family seeks a new start in the Alaskan wilderness, but the father unravels; readers find it gripping and emotional.

handmaids tale.title: The Handmaid's Tale
handmaids tale.author: Margaret Atwood
handmaids tale.why: In a theocratic America women are reduced to childbearing; chilling, widely recommended dystopia.

magus.title: The Magus
magus.author: John Fowles
magus.why: A young teacher on a Greek island is drawn into an elaborate psychological game; readers call it a crazy, gripping mystery.

hike.title: The Hike
hike.author: Drew Magary
hike.why: A man on a walk in the woods enters a surreal world of monsters and puzzles; quick and wildly inventive.

idiot.title: The Idiot
idiot.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
idiot.why: A kind prince returns to Russian society and everything around him turns tragic; some readers find it funny; long and demanding.

atmosphere.title: Atmosphere
atmosphere.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
atmosphere.why: A love story set among women astronauts in the early shuttle era; popular and easy to read.

buffalo hunter hunter.title: The Buffalo Hunter Hunter
buffalo hunter hunter.author: Stephen Graham Jones
buffalo hunter hunter.why: A priest's journals from the 1910s describe a vampire in Montana and the Blackfeet nation; an excellent, unsettling horror novel.

atonement.title: Atonement
atonement.author: Ian McEwan
atonement.why: A child's false accusation wrecks lives, and she spends her life atoning; admired for its ending, though a few readers find it slow.

oryx and crake.title: Oryx and Crake
oryx and crake.author: Margaret Atwood
oryx and crake.why: A lone survivor recalls the genetic engineering world that ended humanity; sharp dystopia that starts the MaddAddam trilogy.

remarkably bright creatures.title: Remarkably Bright Creatures
remarkably bright creatures.author: Shelby Van Pelt
remarkably bright creatures.why: A widow befriends a clever aquarium octopus who knows a secret; a heartwarming, easy read.

cats cradle.title: Cat's Cradle
cats cradle.author: Kurt Vonnegut
cats cradle.why: A writer searches for the inventor of the atom bomb and finds a made-up religion; short, dark and funny.

ishmael.title: Ishmael
ishmael.author: Daniel Quinn
ishmael.why: The comments mostly mix it up with another book of the same name, so there is no clear recommendation.

bluest eye.title: The Bluest Eye
bluest eye.author: Toni Morrison
bluest eye.why: A Black girl in 1940s Ohio longs for blue eyes; short and painful, often recommended for its beautiful prose.

say nothing.title: Say Nothing
say nothing.author: Patrick Radden Keefe
say nothing.why: The story of a woman taken during the Northern Ireland Troubles and the people behind her murder; gripping and surprising narrative history.

recursion.title: Recursion
recursion.author: Blake Crouch
recursion.why: A memory-altering disease and a time device unravel reality; a fast thriller that suckers readers in.

verity.title: Verity
verity.author: Colleen Hoover
verity.why: A writer finishing another author's series finds a disturbing manuscript; an addictive, trashy thriller that kept readers up.

mistborn.title: Mistborn: The Final Empire
mistborn.author: Brandon Sanderson
mistborn.why: A street thief joins a crew to overthrow an immortal ruler using metal-based magic; inventive and fast, with a great twist.

picture of dorian gray.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
picture of dorian gray.author: Oscar Wilde
picture of dorian gray.why: The comments are mostly negative, with readers annoyed or giving up early.

tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.author: Gabrielle Zevin
tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.why: Two friends build video games across decades; warm and moving story about creativity and friendship.

anxious people.title: Anxious People
anxious people.author: Fredrik Backman
anxious people.why: A failed bank robbery turns into a hostage situation at an apartment viewing; comic and warm.

covenant of water.title: The Covenant of Water
covenant of water.author: Abraham Verghese
covenant of water.why: Three generations of a Kerala family linked by a curse and by medicine; long, rich and beautifully written.

all systems red.title: All Systems Red
all systems red.author: Martha Wells
all systems red.why: A security robot hacks its own controls and just wants to watch shows; short, charming and quick to read.

song of achilles.title: The Song of Achilles
song of achilles.author: Madeline Miller
song of achilles.why: The love story of Achilles and Patroclus at Troy, told by Patroclus; readers find it beautiful and heartbreaking.

misery.title: Misery
misery.author: Stephen King
misery.why: A writer is held captive by his number one fan; a tight, scary thriller recommended to anyone starting with King.

shining.title: The Shining
shining.author: Stephen King
shining.why: A struggling writer takes a winter caretaker job at an isolated hotel; the novel is scarier than the film.

martyr.title: Martyr!
martyr.author: Kaveh Akbar
martyr.why: A recovering addict and poet searches for meaning in death; readers rate it highly as a recent standout.

snow crash.title: Snow Crash
snow crash.author: Neal Stephenson
snow crash.why: A pizza-delivering hacker fights a virus in the metaverse; funny, fast-moving cyberpunk.

giver.title: The Giver
giver.author: Lois Lowry
giver.why: A boy discovers the secret behind his perfectly controlled community; a short school favourite that adults say they would re-read.

wild.title: Wild
wild.author: Cheryl Strayed
wild.why: After her mother's death and her marriage collapse, the author hikes the Pacific Crest Trail; moving and beautifully written.

giovannis room.title: Giovanni's Room
giovannis room.author: James Baldwin
giovannis room.why: An American in Paris struggles with desire and shame; short and intense, readers say it blew them away.

lathe of heaven.title: The Lathe of Heaven
lathe of heaven.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
lathe of heaven.why: A man whose dreams change reality has a therapist who wants to use them; a short, odd, thoughtful book.

perdido street station.title: Perdido Street Station
perdido street station.author: China Miéville
perdido street station.why: A scientist unleashes a monster in the strange city of New Crobuzon; dense, inventive new weird fantasy.

long walk.title: The Long Walk
long walk.author: Stephen King
long walk.why: Teenage boys must keep walking in a deadly contest; short, relentless and bleak, and one reader said it hit them hard.

hamnet.title: Hamnet
hamnet.author: Maggie O'Farrell
hamnet.why: Shakespeare's wife and the death of their son, told in lyrical prose; readers say it made them cry.

suttree.title: Suttree
suttree.author: Cormac McCarthy
suttree.why: A man who abandoned his family lives among drifters on the Tennessee river; dense, bleak and darkly funny McCarthy.

his dark materials.title: His Dark Materials
his dark materials.author: Philip Pullman
his dark materials.why: A girl travels between worlds in a fight against a powerful church; a children's trilogy that adults love.

sound and the fury.title: The Sound and the Fury
sound and the fury.author: William Faulkner
sound and the fury.why: The decline of a Southern family told through four voices, one of them mentally disabled; famously hard but admired.

betty.title: Betty
betty.author: Tiffany McDaniel
betty.why: A girl grows up in Ohio in a troubled Cherokee family and learns through stories; readers say they sobbed through the ending.

lord of light.title: Lord of Light
lord of light.author: Roger Zelazny
lord of light.why: Space colonists live as Hindu gods on a distant planet, and one rebels; mythic, stylish and often listed among the best.

jane eyre.title: Jane Eyre
jane eyre.author: Charlotte Brontë
jane eyre.why: An orphan becomes a governess and falls for her mysterious employer; romantic, gothic and recommended as an accessible classic.

klara and the sun.title: Klara and the Sun
klara and the sun.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
klara and the sun.why: A solar-powered robot companion watches over a sick girl; quietly moving and hard to put down.

silent patient.title: The Silent Patient
silent patient.author: Alex Michaelides
silent patient.why: A woman stops speaking after killing her husband and a therapist tries to understand why; a quick thriller with a twist.

ancillary justice.title: Ancillary Justice
ancillary justice.author: Ann Leckie
ancillary justice.why: A former starship AI in a single human body seeks revenge; clever space opera that sticks to its sequels.

god of the woods.title: The God of the Woods
god of the woods.author: Liz Moore
god of the woods.why: A child disappears from a summer camp, decades after her brother vanished; a twisty mystery that readers are enjoying.

passage.title: The Passage
passage.author: Justin Cronin
passage.why: A government experiment turns people into vampires and the survivors face an apocalyptic world; long and compelling.

correspondent.title: The Correspondent
correspondent.author: Virginia Evans
correspondent.why: A retired woman keeps up her life through letters; readers say they loved it so much they re-read it.

reformatory.title: The Reformatory
reformatory.author: Tananarive Due
reformatory.why: A boy is sent to a brutal 1950s Florida reform school haunted by the dead; a powerful horror novel rooted in history.

house in the cerulean sea.title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
house in the cerulean sea.author: T. J. Klune
house in the cerulean sea.why: A caseworker inspects an orphanage of magical children and finds a home; warm, gentle and uplifting.

hot zone.title: The Hot Zone
hot zone.author: Richard Preston
hot zone.why: A real account of an Ebola-like virus outbreak near Washington; terrifying and gripping.

jonathan strange and mr norrell.title: Jonathan Strange and Mr. Norrell
jonathan strange and mr norrell.author: Susanna Clarke
jonathan strange and mr norrell.why: Two magicians return English magic in the Napoleonic era; long, dry-witted alternate history that readers get absorbed in.

room.title: Room
room.author: Emma Donoghue
room.why: A five-year-old narrator lives in one room with his mother; a disturbing but compelling and moving story.

jungle.title: The Jungle
jungle.author: Upton Sinclair
jungle.why: Immigrant workers in Chicago's meatpacking industry face hardship; relentlessly bleak and an important muckraking novel.

hatchet.title: Hatchet
hatchet.author: Gary Paulsen
hatchet.why: A boy survives alone in the Canadian wilderness after a plane crash; a quick, easy adventure that kids and adults remember.

invisible man.title: Invisible Man
invisible man.author: Ralph Ellison
invisible man.why: A Black man moves through America feeling unseen; powerful, demanding and often described as a missed classic.

cloud atlas.title: Cloud Atlas
cloud atlas.author: David Mitchell
cloud atlas.why: Six nested stories in different eras and styles echo each other; ambitious and frequently named a favourite.

use of weapons.title: Use of Weapons
use of weapons.author: Iain Banks
use of weapons.why: A mercenary's two timelines run in opposite directions toward a revelation; many Banks fans name it his best.

wasp factory.title: The Wasp Factory
wasp factory.author: Iain Banks
wasp factory.why: A teenage boy's cruel rituals on a remote Scottish island hide a shocking secret; short and truly horrifying.

lincoln in the bardo.title: Lincoln in the Bardo
lincoln in the bardo.author: George Saunders
lincoln in the bardo.why: Ghosts crowd a graveyard after Lincoln's son dies; experimental, voiced chorus that moves many readers.

trust.title: Trust
trust.author: Hernán Díaz
trust.why: Four versions of a 1920s financier's story reveal different truths; readers find it amazing and easy to enjoy.

hearts invisible furies.title: The Heart's Invisible Furies
hearts invisible furies.author: John Boyne
hearts invisible furies.why: A gay man's life in Ireland from birth across seven decades; a sweeping book that readers love.

middlesex.title: Middlesex
middlesex.author: Jeffrey Eugenides
middlesex.why: A Greek-American family saga narrated by an intersex person; multigenerational and warmly told.

invisible life of addie larue.title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
invisible life of addie larue.author: V. E. Schwab
invisible life of addie larue.why: A woman makes a deal to live forever but be forgotten; romantic and lyrical, liked by many readers.

sirens of titan.title: The Sirens of Titan
sirens of titan.author: Kurt Vonnegut
sirens of titan.why: The richest man on Earth is pulled into a cosmic joke of a plan; a darkly funny early Vonnegut.

kite runner.title: The Kite Runner
kite runner.author: Khaled Hosseini
kite runner.why: A man in America tries to atone for a childhood betrayal in Afghanistan; readers say it lives up to the hype.

between two fires.title: Between two fires
between two fires.author: Christopher Buehlman
between two fires.why: A knight and a girl cross plague-ridden France in the 1300s as angels and demons clash; readers are engrossed.

prophet song.title: Prophet Song
prophet song.author: Paul Lynch
prophet song.why: A Dublin mother copes as Ireland slides into authoritarianism; relentless unpunctuated prose that readers call gripping.

normal people.title: Normal People
normal people.author: Sally Rooney
normal people.why: Two Irish teens drift together and apart for years; spare, intense, and one reader admitted to re-reading at once.

les miserables.title: Les Misérables
les miserables.author: Victor Hugo
les miserables.why: An ex-convict tries to live a good life in 19th-century France; a huge, powerful and humane classic.

wild dark shore.title: Wild Dark Shore
wild dark shore.author: Charlotte McConaghy
wild dark shore.why: A family lives on a remote island that is near the Antarctic, with a mystery washed ashore; readers love it.

enders game.title: Ender's Game
enders game.author: Orson Scott Card
enders game.why: A gifted boy is trained at a space military school; a classic page-turner that readers recommend for military sci-fi.

magic mountain.title: The Magic Mountain
magic mountain.author: Thomas Mann
magic mountain.why: A young man visits a sanatorium and stays for seven years; slow, philosophical and rewarding.

boys life.title: Boy's life
boys life.author: Robert R. McCammon
boys life.why: A boy in 1960s Alabama sees a murder and grows up with mystery and magic; a nostalgic coming-of-age favourite.

all the light we cannot see.title: All the Light We Cannot See
all the light we cannot see.author: Anthony Doerr
all the light we cannot see.why: A blind French girl and a German boy meet in the war; short chapters and lyrical prose make it a popular pick.

sabriel.title: Sabriel
sabriel.author: Garth Nix
sabriel.why: A young necromancer enters the Old Kingdom to save her father; an excellent dark fantasy aimed at teens and adults.

know my name.title: Know My Name
know my name.author: Chanel Miller
know my name.why: The woman once known as Emily Doe tells her own story after a sexual assault trial; powerful and painful.

solaris.title: Solaris
solaris.author: Stanisław Lem
solaris.why: Scientists orbit a planet that seems to read their minds; Lem's cerebral first-contact classic.

historian.title: The Historian
historian.author: Elizabeth Kostova
historian.why: A young woman follows her father's trail across Europe in search of Dracula; slow-burning gothic mystery.

old man and the sea.title: The Old Man and the Sea
old man and the sea.author: Ernest Hemingway
old man and the sea.why: An aged fisherman battles a huge marlin for days; short and simple, readers say it is deep.

cloud cuckoo land.title: Cloud Cuckoo Land
cloud cuckoo land.author: Anthony Doerr
cloud cuckoo land.why: Linked stories across centuries and a lost ancient book; warm and ambitious like his earlier hit.

their eyes were watching god.title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
their eyes were watching god.author: Zora Neale Hurston
their eyes were watching god.why: A Black woman in Florida seeks love and her own voice; lyrical and pretty widely recommended.

war and peace.title: War and Peace
war and peace.author: Leo Tolstoy
war and peace.why: Five families live through the Napoleonic wars in Russia; a huge book readers say becomes absorbing.

cryptonomicon.title: Cryptonomicon
cryptonomicon.author: Neal Stephenson
cryptonomicon.why: Codebreakers in World War II and hackers today pursue a hidden treasure; long, geeky and funny, with a beloved character.

tampa.title: Tampa
tampa.author: Alissa Nutting
tampa.why: A teacher abuses her students and narrates her own predation; very disturbing yet a page turner according to readers.

animal farm.title: Animal Farm
animal farm.author: George Orwell
animal farm.why: Farm animals overthrow their master and a new tyranny arises; a short allegory still read widely.

long way to a small angry planet.title: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
long way to a small angry planet.author: Becky Chambers
long way to a small angry planet.why: A mixed-species crew travels on a tunnelling ship; warm, character-driven space adventure.

catch 22.title: Catch-22
catch 22.author: Joseph Heller
catch 22.why: A bomber pilot tries to escape the army's absurd rules; a funny, memorable war satire.

tainted cup.title: The Tainted Cup
tainted cup.author: Robert Jackson Bennett
tainted cup.why: A detective and her assistant investigate a murder in a world with giant monsters; blends mystery and fantasy well.

naked lunch.title: Naked Lunch
naked lunch.author: William S. Burroughs
naked lunch.why: The comments describe it as unpleasant or the worst book they read, so it is not a recommendation.

starter villain.title: Starter Villain
starter villain.author: John Scalzi
starter villain.why: A substitute teacher inherits his uncle's supervillain empire; a short and breezy comic romp.

dhalgren.title: Dhalgren
dhalgren.author: Samuel R. Delany
dhalgren.why: An amnesiac wanders a ruined American city; long and strange, loved by experimental sci-fi fans.

to say nothing of the dog.title: To Say Nothing of the Dog
to say nothing of the dog.author: Connie Willis
to say nothing of the dog.why: Time-travelling historians are sent to Victorian England to find a missing object; comic and charming.

gideon the ninth.title: Gideon the Ninth
gideon the ninth.author: Tamsyn Muir
gideon the ninth.why: A swordswoman and a necromancer enter a haunted space house; gothic and joking, and readers keep going to the sequels.

on the road.title: On The Road
on the road.author: Jack Kerouac
on the road.why: Friends hit the road across 1950s America; changed some readers' lives and bored others.

memory police.title: The Memory Police
memory police.author: Yōko Ogawa
memory police.why: On an island things disappear and people forget them; quiet dystopia that people recommend.

last unicorn.title: The Last Unicorn
last unicorn.author: Peter S. Beagle
last unicorn.why: A unicorn leaves her forest to find others like her; a lyrical, bittersweet fairy tale.

starless sea.title: The Starless Sea
starless sea.author: Erin Morgenstern
starless sea.why: A graduate student finds a book that leads to an underground library; pretty, dreamy and loved.

foundation.title: Foundation
foundation.author: Isaac Asimov
foundation.why: A mathematician predicts the fall of a galactic empire and plans to save knowledge; a classic of ideas.

heart of darkness.title: Heart of Darkness
heart of darkness.author: Joseph Conrad
heart of darkness.why: A steamboat captain travels upriver in the Congo toward the sinister Kurtz; short and dense, widely read.

gone world.title: The Gone World
gone world.author: Tom Sweterlitsch
gone world.why: A time-travelling investigator hunts a killer in a future that is ending; a gripping hybrid of thriller and sci-fi.

small things like these.title: Small Things Like These
small things like these.author: Claire Keegan
small things like these.why: A coal merchant in 1985 Ireland finds a secret at a convent; a very short, quietly powerful novel.

sea of tranquility.title: Sea of Tranquility
sea of tranquility.author: Emily St. John Mandel
sea of tranquility.why: Linked lives across centuries are connected by a strange glitch in time; a short and elegant favourite.

haunted.title: Haunted
haunted.author: Chuck Palahniuk
haunted.why: Writers at a retreat tell grotesque stories while isolated; shocking, fun and awful in readers' words.

salems lot.title: 'Salem’s Lot
salems lot.author: Stephen King
salems lot.why: Vampires take over a small Maine town; readers call it an absolute classic of horror.

my brilliant friend.title: My Brilliant Friend
my brilliant friend.author: Elena Ferrante
my brilliant friend.why: The intense friendship of two girls growing up in postwar Naples; the first Neapolitan novel and a widely praised read.

frozen river.title: The Frozen River
frozen river.author: Ariel Lawhon
frozen river.why: A midwife investigates a death in 1789 Maine, based on a real diary; readers named it a top read.

severance.title: Severance
severance.author: Ling Ma
severance.why: A plague turns people into zombie-like routines while an office worker keeps going; funny and sad, called brilliant.

on the beach.title: On the Beach
on the beach.author: Nevil Shute
on the beach.why: People in Australia wait calmly for radiation from nuclear war to arrive; a quiet and moving apocalypse story.

dog stars.title: The Dog Stars
dog stars.author: Peter Heller
dog stars.why: A pilot and his dog survive after a pandemic; lyrical post-apocalypse that readers recommend.

trial.title: The Trial
trial.author: Franz Kafka
trial.why: The comments mostly say they disliked it or are just partway through, so nobody clearly recommends it.

expanse.title: Leviathan Wakes
expanse.author: James S. A. Corey
expanse.why: A ship crew uncovers a plot that may start a war across the solar system; realistic, gripping space opera.

odyssey.title: The Odyssey
odyssey.author: Homer
odyssey.why: Odysseus struggles for ten years to get home; the foundation of adventure storytelling, readers value modern translations.

holes.title: Holes
holes.author: Louis Sachar
holes.why: A boy is sent to dig holes at a desert camp and learns its secret; clever and fast, loved since childhood.

good earth.title: The Good Earth
good earth.author: Pearl S. Buck
good earth.why: A Chinese peasant farmer's rise and the ups and downs of his family across years; a classic family saga.

embassytown.title: Embassytown
embassytown.author: China Miéville
embassytown.why: Humans on an alien world depend on a language in which one cannot lie; one reader's best ever.

spear cuts through water.title: The Spear Cuts Through Water
spear cuts through water.author: Simon Jimenez
spear cuts through water.why: A boy and a woman journey through a mythic empire; poetic and moving, with unusual storytelling.

johnny got his gun.title: Johnny Got His Gun
johnny got his gun.author: Dalton Trumbo
johnny got his gun.why: A soldier maimed in World War I is trapped in his own mind; short and harrowing antiwar book.

diaspora.title: Diaspora
diaspora.author: Greg Egan
diaspora.why: Digital citizens and robots spread across the galaxy to avoid a cosmic threat; hard sci-fi with intense ideas.

american psycho.title: American Psycho
american psycho.author: Bret Easton Ellis
american psycho.why: A wealthy 1980s banker narrates his casual murders; very graphic and satirical, giving readers nightmares.

fairy tale.title: Fairy Tale
fairy tale.author: Stephen King
fairy tale.why: A teenager inherits a secret portal to another world in his neighbour's shed; readers say they did not want it to end.

shantaram.title: Shantaram
shantaram.author: Gregory David Roberts
shantaram.why: A fugitive hides in Bombay and falls in with the underworld; a long, immersive tale based on the author's life.

childhoods end.title: Childhood's End
childhoods end.author: Arthur C. Clarke
childhoods end.why: Peaceful alien overlords arrive and change humanity's future; short and thought-provoking classic.

nickel boys.title: The Nickel Boys
nickel boys.author: Colson Whitehead
nickel boys.why: Two Black teens suffer in a brutal Florida reform school; spare and devastating with not a word wasted.

city of thieves.title: City of Thieves
city of thieves.author: David Benioff
city of thieves.why: Two young men must find a dozen eggs during the Siege of Leningrad; fast, funny and heartfelt.

foster.title: Foster
foster.author: Claire Keegan
foster.why: A neglected girl is sent to live with relatives in rural Ireland; a short, quietly moving story.

yesteryear.title: Yesteryear
yesteryear.author: Caro Claire Burke
yesteryear.why: A tradwife influencer wakes up in the past; recommended by readers eager for it, though few have finished it.

underworld.title: Underworld
underworld.author: Don DeLillo
underworld.why: American life from the Cold War onward, built around a baseball; astonishing, ambitious and demanding.

magicians.title: The Magicians
magicians.author: Lev Grossman
magicians.why: A student finds a secret magic college that is not as good as the Narnia of his dreams; darker and sharper.

ubik.title: Ubik
ubik.author: Philip K. Dick
ubik.why: Reality begins to decay around a team of psychic-detecting agents; short, weird and typically Dick.

atlas shrugged.title: Atlas Shrugged
atlas shrugged.author: Ayn Rand
atlas shrugged.why: It is only named as something the commenters tried or warned about, with little actual recommendation.

orbital.title: Orbital
orbital.author: Samantha Harvey
orbital.why: The comments are more critical than positive; one reader finds it irritating and another has not yet read it.

push.title: The Push
push.author: Ashley Audrain
push.why: A woman fears her daughter has something wrong with her; a disturbing psychological thriller about motherhood.

lapvona.title: Lapvona
lapvona.author: Ottessa Moshfegh
lapvona.why: A medieval village suffers famine and cruelty; terrifying and grotesque and loved by the reader.

beartown.title: Beartown
beartown.author: Fredrik Backman
beartown.why: A hockey town splits after a crime; readers say it is the Backman they will always name first.

jurassic park.title: Jurassic Park
jurassic park.author: Michael Crichton
jurassic park.why: Cloned dinosaurs run wild on a theme-park island; a fast techno-thriller that beats the film.

things they carried.title: The Things They Carried
things they carried.author: Tim O'Brien
things they carried.why: Linked stories about soldiers in the Vietnam War, what they carry and what they tell; widely taught and often reread.

contact.title: Contact
contact.author: Carl Sagan
contact.why: A scientist receives a message from space and must decide what it means; readers sit stunned after finishing it.

pride and prejudice.title: Pride and Prejudice
pride and prejudice.author: Jane Austen
pride and prejudice.why: Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy fight pride on the way to love; readers return decades later and still enjoy it.

life.title: Life
life.author: Keith Richards
life.why: The comments do not discuss this memoir; they are about other books, so the match is wrong.

crossing.title: The Crossing
crossing.author: Cormac McCarthy
crossing.why: A boy crosses into Mexico several times, with a wolf and a loss; sublime, spare and demanding in his pace.

stars my destination.title: The Stars My Destination
stars my destination.author: Alfred Bester
stars my destination.why: A vengeful man with strange powers pursues rich enemies across the solar system; a classic that drags readers along.

forever war.title: The Forever War
forever war.author: Joe Haldeman
forever war.why: A soldier fights an interstellar war while time dilation leaves him lost at home; short and reality-minded military sci-fi.

to the lighthouse.title: To the Lighthouse
to the lighthouse.author: Virginia Woolf
to the lighthouse.why: A family holiday on a Scottish island unfolds through shifting inner thoughts; lyrical but demanding.

enchanted forest chronicles.title: The Enchanted Forest Chronicles
enchanted forest chronicles.author: Patricia C. Wrede
enchanted forest chronicles.why: A princess who dislikes being a princess goes to live with dragons; funny, clever children's fantasy fondly remembered.

of mice and men.title: Of Mice and Men
of mice and men.author: John Steinbeck
of mice and men.why: Two migrant workers dream of a farm of their own; very short and heartbreaking.

lottery.title: The Lottery
lottery.author: Shirley Jackson
lottery.why: A small town holds its yearly ritual; a very short, shocking story whose tropes started here.

unbroken.title: Unbroken
unbroken.author: Laura Hillenbrand
unbroken.why: An Olympic runner survives a plane crash, the sea and a prison camp in World War II; a testament to the will to live.

as i lay dying.title: As I Lay Dying
as i lay dying.author: William Faulkner
as i lay dying.why: A poor Southern family carries their mother's coffin to burial through a series of voices; short but difficult.

suitable boy.title: A Suitable Boy
suitable boy.author: Vikram Seth
suitable boy.why: A mother in newly independent India searches for a husband for her daughter; a huge, absorbing family novel.

seven husbands of evelyn hugo.title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
seven husbands of evelyn hugo.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
seven husbands of evelyn hugo.why: An old film star tells a young journalist about her many marriages; easy and addictive, recommended widely.

murder of roger ackroyd.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
murder of roger ackroyd.author: Agatha Christie
murder of roger ackroyd.why: Poirot investigates a village murder with a famous twist; readers love it and its ending.

wolf hall.title: Wolf Hall
wolf hall.author: Hilary Mantel
wolf hall.why: Thomas Cromwell rises in Henry VIII's court; rich and intense, though the style is demanding.

true grit.title: True Grit
true grit.author: Charles Portis
true grit.why: A girl hires a rough marshal to find her father's killer; sharp-voiced, funny western.

all the colors of the dark.title: All the Colors of the Dark
all the colors of the dark.author: Chris Whitaker
all the colors of the dark.why: A long mystery about a missing girl in 1970s Missouri; readers are drawn in by its characters.

everlasting.title: The Everlasting
everlasting.author: Alix E. Harrow
everlasting.why: A historian cursed to relive a king's life shapes history across time; could not be put down according to readers.

david copperfield.title: David Copperfield
david copperfield.author: Charles Dickens
david copperfield.why: A boy's rise from a hard childhood to novelist; warm, long Dickens with many memorable characters.

troop.title: The troop
troop.author: Nick Cutter
troop.why: Boy scouts on a remote island face a horrifying infection; gruesome and fast, a repeat read for horror fans.

house of suns.title: House of Suns
house of suns.author: Alastair Reynolds
house of suns.why: Clones of one person travel the galaxy and meet a threat; vast space opera readers return to.

four winds.title: The Four Winds
four winds.author: Kristin Hannah
four winds.why: A Texas family struggles in the Dust Bowl, especially the second half; emotional and popular.

monster calls.title: A Monster Calls
monster calls.author: Patrick Ness
monster calls.why: A boy facing his mother's illness is visited by a tree monster; short and moving, best in the illustrated edition.

wedding people.title: The Wedding People
wedding people.author: Alison Espach
wedding people.why: A woman crashes a wedding at a hotel while at a low point; light, funny and heartfelt.

fourth wing.title: Fourth Wing
fourth wing.author: Rebecca Yarros
fourth wing.why: A frail woman enters a war college where cadets bond with dragons; polarising but a binge read for fans.

on earth were briefly gorgeous.title: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous
on earth were briefly gorgeous.author: Ocean Vuong
on earth were briefly gorgeous.why: A son writes to his mother who cannot read, about family and violence; a lyrical, short debut by a poet.

gone away world.title: The Gone-Away World
gone away world.author: Nick Harkaway
gone away world.why: After a war that destroyed reality, a man travels to put out a fire; funny and odd.

in search of lost time.title: In Search of Lost Time
in search of lost time.author: Marcel Proust
in search of lost time.why: A narrator reflects on memory, love and society across seven volumes; famously long and demanding yet widely revered.

dubliners.title: Dubliners
dubliners.author: James Joyce
dubliners.why: Fifteen stories of ordinary life in Dublin; short and precise, ending with a famous long one.

artemis.title: Artemis
artemis.author: Andy Weir
artemis.why: The comments are lukewarm or compare it unfavorably, so it is not a clear recommendation.

indifferent stars above.title: The Indifferent Stars Above
indifferent stars above.author: Daniel James Brown
indifferent stars above.why: The true story of the Donner Party's ill-fated overland journey; recommended as a non-fiction page-turner.

tress of the emerald sea.title: Tress of the Emerald Sea
tress of the emerald sea.author: Brandon Sanderson
tress of the emerald sea.why: A girl sails a sea of spores to rescue the boy she loves; whimsical and charming.

american gods.title: American Gods
american gods.author: Neil Gaiman
american gods.why: Old gods fight new ones in modern America; a solid road-trip novel that many prefer to the TV series.

fingersmith.title: Fingersmith
fingersmith.author: Sarah Waters
fingersmith.why: Victorian pickpockets and a heiress get mixed in a plot with major twists; a favourite of many readers.

old mans war.title: Old Man’s War
old mans war.author: John Scalzi
old mans war.why: Seniors join the army to fight aliens in new young bodies; quick and fun, though sequels weaken.

ministry of time.title: The Ministry of Time
ministry of time.author: Kaliane Bradley
ministry of time.why: A civil servant looks after a man from Franklin's lost expedition brought to the present; a time-travel romance.

just kids.title: Just Kids
just kids.author: Patti Smith
just kids.why: The singer's tender memoir of her friendship with Robert Mapplethorpe in 1970s New York; moving and beautifully written.

catcher in the rye.title: The Catcher in the Rye
catcher in the rye.author: J. D. Salinger
catcher in the rye.why: A teenage boy wanders New York after leaving school; a short coming-of-age classic readers still enjoy.

sharp objects.title: Sharp Objects
sharp objects.author: Gillian Flynn
sharp objects.why: A reporter returns to her hometown to cover murders and confronts her family; a gripping, disturbing thriller.

things fall apart.title: Things Fall Apart
things fall apart.author: Chinua Achebe
things fall apart.why: A proud Igbo man's world is upended by colonisers; short and powerful, often read as an answer to colonial fiction.

good omens.title: Good Omens
good omens.author: Terry Pratchett
good omens.why: An angel and a demon try to stop the apocalypse because they like Earth; hilarious and widely loved.

stranger in a strange land.title: Stranger in a Strange Land
stranger in a strange land.author: Robert A. Heinlein
stranger in a strange land.why: A human raised by Martians returns to Earth and shakes up its customs; a famous, provocative counterculture classic.

child of god.title: Child of God
child of god.author: Cormac McCarthy
child of god.why: A violent outcast lives in the Tennessee hills; short and harrowing, for readers who can handle disturbing McCarthy.

meditations.title: Meditations
meditations.author: Marcus Aurelius
meditations.why: The Roman emperor's private notes on duty, calm and death; readers value its practical stoic advice.

immortal life of henrietta lacks.title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
immortal life of henrietta lacks.author: Rebecca Skloot
immortal life of henrietta lacks.why: The story of the woman whose cells were taken without consent and used in science; moving and informative.

candide.title: Candide
candide.author: Voltaire
candide.why: A naive young man travels through disaster after disaster while told that all is for the best; short and biting.

butter.title: Butter
butter.author: Asako Yuzuki
butter.why: A journalist becomes obsessed with a gourmet woman convicted of murder; food, gender and appetite make it hard to stop.

shark heart.title: Shark Heart
shark heart.author: Emily Habeck
shark heart.why: A man is slowly turning into a shark as his wife prepares to lose him; strange, tender and loved by readers.

curse of chalion.title: The Curse of Chalion
curse of chalion.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
curse of chalion.why: A broken soldier becomes tutor to a princess in a kingdom cursed by gods; deeply human and well liked.

blade itself.title: The Blade Itself
blade itself.author: Joe Abercrombie
blade itself.why: A torturer, a barbarian and a vain swordsman are drawn into a war; grim and funny, the start of The First Law.

you.title: You
you.author: Caroline Kepnes
you.why: A bookstore clerk stalks a woman and tells it as love; creepy, addictive thriller.

assassins apprentice.title: Assassin's Apprentice
assassins apprentice.author: Robin Hobb
assassins apprentice.why: A royal bastard is trained as a secret killer; slow-building and emotional, the first Farseer book.

nothing to see here.title: Nothing to See Here
nothing to see here.author: Kevin Wilson
nothing to see here.why: A woman becomes nanny to two children who burst into flames; absurd, warm and quick, making readers laugh out loud.

mrs dalloway.title: Mrs. Dalloway
mrs dalloway.author: Virginia Woolf
mrs dalloway.why: One day in the life of a London woman and a shell-shocked soldier; stream of consciousness that some love.

scanner darkly.title: A Scanner Darkly
scanner darkly.author: Philip K. Dick
scanner darkly.why: An undercover agent addicted to a drug watches himself; paranoid and sad, someone's comfort book.

finnegans wake.title: Finnegans Wake
finnegans wake.author: James Joyce
finnegans wake.why: The comments describe it as unread or too hard, not recommended.

corrections.title: The Corrections
corrections.author: Jonathan Franzen
corrections.why: A midwestern family comes together for a last Christmas; funny and moving, though compared to DeLillo.

collector.title: The Collector
collector.author: John Fowles
collector.why: A lonely man kidnaps a young woman and keeps her in his cellar; a short, chilling psychological novel.

midnights children.title: Midnight's Children
midnights children.author: Salman Rushdie
midnights children.why: A man born at India's independence is linked to other children with powers; colourful and demanding magical realism.

ice.title: Ice
ice.author: Anna Kavan
ice.why: A narrator chases a girl through a world freezing under ice; short, dreamlike and experimental.

player of games.title: The player of games
player of games.author: Iain Banks
player of games.why: A game master is sent to play an alien empire's brutal game; a smart and approachable Culture novel.

hunger.title: Hunger
hunger.author: Knut Hamsun
hunger.why: The comments mix up several books titled Hunger, so there is no clear recommendation for this one.

howls moving castle.title: Howl's Moving Castle
howls moving castle.author: Diana Wynne Jones
howls moving castle.why: A girl turned into an old woman moves into a wizard's castle; funny and charming, different from the film.

dawn.title: Dawn
dawn.author: Octavia E. Butler
dawn.why: Aliens save the last humans but ask for a price; thoughtful, uneasy and often recommended.

roots.title: Roots
roots.author: Alex Haley
roots.why: A family saga from an African village into American slavery; readers say it is one of the most powerful books they read.

girl next door.title: The Girl Next Door
girl next door.author: Jack Ketchum
girl next door.why: A teenager is tortured by her guardian and neighbourhood kids in 1950s suburbia; the book that broke readers, with an extremely disturbing story.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.author: Marilynne Robinson
gilead.why: An elderly minister writes a long letter to his young son; quiet, spiritual and beautifully written.

princess bride.title: The Princess Bride
princess bride.author: William Goldman
princess bride.why: A farm boy, a princess and a swordfight through fairy-tale perils; witty and loved even more than the movie.

wool.title: Wool
wool.author: Hugh Howey
wool.why: People live in an underground silo and the sheriff wants the truth; gripping with twists, and the basis of Silo.

jitterbug perfume.title: Jitterbug Perfume
jitterbug perfume.author: Tom Robbins
jitterbug perfume.why: A quest for the secret of immortality involving beets, perfume and gods; a funny, quirky book readers re-read yearly.

poppy war.title: The Poppy War
poppy war.author: R. F. Kuang
poppy war.why: A war orphan wins a place at an elite military school and discovers shamanic power; brutal, exceptional start to a series.

great believers.title: The Great Believers
great believers.author: Rebecca Makkai
great believers.why: Friends in 1980s Chicago face the AIDS crisis, and one's daughter searches for her family in 2015; left readers shattered.

pet sematary.title: Pet Sematary
pet sematary.author: Stephen King
pet sematary.why: A family finds a burial ground that brings the dead back; one of the bleakest King novels.

our wives under the sea.title: Our Wives Under the Sea
our wives under the sea.author: Julia Armfield
our wives under the sea.why: A wife returns from a deep-sea mission changed; short, strange and lyrical.

consider phlebas.title: Consider Phlebas
consider phlebas.author: Iain Banks
consider phlebas.why: A shape-shifter spy joins a war between the Culture and its enemies; big, action-driven space opera.

prince of tides.title: The Prince of Tides
prince of tides.author: Pat Conroy
prince of tides.why: A southern man confronts his family's secrets with his sister's psychiatrist; a long, emotional Southern novel.

awakening.title: The Awakening
awakening.author: Kate Chopin
awakening.why: A wife in 1890s Louisiana seeks independence; short and ahead of its time, and some readers say it changed their life.

king sorrow.title: King Sorrow
king sorrow.author: Joe Hill
king sorrow.why: The comments only say people are starting it, so there is no recommendation yet.

lies of locke lamora.title: The Lies of Locke Lamora
lies of locke lamora.author: Scott Lynch
lies of locke lamora.why: A gang of thieves in a Venice-like city gets pulled into a deadly plot; fast, funny fantasy heist and five-star read.

phantom tollbooth.title: The Phantom Tollbooth
phantom tollbooth.author: Norton Juster
phantom tollbooth.why: A bored boy drives into a land of puns and wordplay; clever, loved children's fantasy.

crying in h mart.title: Crying in H Mart
crying in h mart.author: Michelle Zauner
crying in h mart.why: The musician writes about losing her mother and her Korean heritage through food; moving and easy to read.

great gatsby.title: The Great Gatsby
great gatsby.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
great gatsby.why: A mysterious millionaire throws parties to win back his love in Jazz Age New York; short and beautifully written.

martian chronicles.title: The Martian Chronicles
martian chronicles.author: Ray Bradbury
martian chronicles.why: Linked stories about humans colonising Mars; lyrical and wistful rather than technical.

dutch house.title: The Dutch House
dutch house.author: Ann Patchett
dutch house.why: A brother and sister are cast out of their family mansion and remain obsessed with it; warm and gently moving.

priory of the orange tree.title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
priory of the orange tree.author: Samantha Shannon
priory of the orange tree.why: Dragons and queens in a standalone high fantasy with a sweeping plot; long but fast.

angelas ashes.title: Angela's Ashes
angelas ashes.author: Frank McCourt
angelas ashes.why: The author's poor Irish childhood in Limerick; sad and often darkly funny, and a bestselling memoir.

great expectations.title: Great Expectations
great expectations.author: Charles Dickens
great expectations.why: An orphan receives a mysterious fortune and learns what matters; one of the most readable Dickens novels.

pretty girls.title: Pretty Girls
pretty girls.author: Karin Slaughter
pretty girls.why: Two sisters uncover secrets about a serial killer; a gripping, graphic thriller that readers could not put down.

uprooted.title: Uprooted
uprooted.author: Naomi Novik
uprooted.why: A village girl is taken by a wizard to fight a corrupted wood; a fairy-tale inspired novel that gets absorbing.

sphere.title: Sphere
sphere.author: Michael Crichton
sphere.why: Scientists investigate a mysterious spacecraft on the ocean floor; long and gripping, though some find it minor Crichton.

emma.title: Emma
emma.author: Jane Austen
emma.why: A well-meaning matchmaker misreads everyone around her; light and witty, and free to read.

little big.title: Little, Big
little big.author: John Crowley
little big.why: A family's connection with fairies unfolds over generations; poetic and strange with a following.

hunger games.title: The Hunger Games
hunger games.author: Suzanne Collins
hunger games.why: A girl volunteers for a televised fight to the death; fast and gripping young-adult dystopia.

sapiens.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
sapiens.author: Yuval Noah Harari
sapiens.why: A broad history of humankind from the cognitive revolution on; readers call it excellent, though some dispute its science.

ministry for the future.title: The Ministry for the Future
ministry for the future.author: Kim Stanley Robinson
ministry for the future.why: A near-future institution works to fight climate change; ideas-heavy and told in many fragments, often recommended.

rejection.title: Rejection
rejection.author: Tony Tulathimutte
rejection.why: Linked stories about people rejected in love and in life; sharp, bold and laugh-out-loud.

night watch.title: Night Watch
night watch.author: Terry Pratchett
night watch.why: Sam Vimes is thrown back to his younger days during a revolt; often named the best Discworld book.

in the dream house.title: In the Dream House
in the dream house.author: Carmen Maria Machado
in the dream house.why: The author's memoir of an abusive relationship, told in short, shifting genre chapters; inventive and powerful.

guards guards.title: Guards! Guards!
guards guards.author: Terry Pratchett
guards guards.why: The Ankh-Morpork night watch faces a dragon; a funny, approachable start to the Watch series.

into the wild.title: Into the Wild
into the wild.author: Jon Krakauer
into the wild.why: The true story of a young man who went alone into Alaska; gripping and often recommended.

iliad.title: The Iliad
iliad.author: Homer
iliad.why: The wrath of Achilles during the siege of Troy; ancient and brutal epic that readers take on in a good translation.

eileen.title: Eileen
eileen.author: Ottessa Moshfegh
eileen.why: A lonely young woman working at a prison in 1960s New England meets a stranger; dark and sharp.

aurora.title: Aurora
aurora.author: Kim Stanley Robinson
aurora.why: One commenter hated it and another is unsure, so there is little clear recommendation.

dandelion wine.title: Dandelion Wine
dandelion wine.author: Ray Bradbury
dandelion wine.why: A boy's summer in 1928 small-town Illinois, full of wonder; nostalgic and lyrical, from a legitimate genius.

crying of lot 49.title: The Crying of Lot 49
crying of lot 49.author: Thomas Pynchon
crying of lot 49.why: A woman uncovers what may be a secret postal conspiracy in California; short, strange and a good first Pynchon.

power.title: The Power
power.author: Naomi Alderman
power.why: Women suddenly gain the ability to shock, flipping the balance of power; compelling and brutal.

mexican gothic.title: Mexican Gothic
mexican gothic.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
mexican gothic.why: A creeping gothic haunted-house story in 1950s Mexico that readers find genuinely disturbing and hard to forget.

intermezzo.title: Intermezzo
intermezzo.author: Sally Rooney
intermezzo.why: Two grieving brothers and the women in their lives, told in Rooney's spare style; fans of her earlier books enjoy it.

thief of always.title: The Thief of Always
thief of always.author: Clive Barker
thief of always.why: A dark fairy tale about a boy who is offered a perfect house of endless holidays and the price attached.

tom lake.title: Tom Lake
tom lake.author: Ann Patchett
tom lake.why: A mother tells her daughters about her youthful acting summer and an old romance; warm and easy, though not for everyone.

bear.title: The bear
bear.author: Andrew Krivak
bear.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

there there.title: There There
there there.author: Tommy Orange
there there.why: Interwoven stories of urban Native Americans in Oakland building toward a powerful finale that left readers in tears.

all the pretty horses.title: All the Pretty Horses
all the pretty horses.author: Cormac McCarthy
all the pretty horses.why: A teenage cowboy rides into Mexico in a lyrical coming-of-age western praised for its beautiful prose.

first fifteen lives of harry august.title: The First Fifteen Lives of Harry August
first fifteen lives of harry august.author: Claire North
first fifteen lives of harry august.why: A man who relives his life again and again investigates a threat to the world in a clever take on immortality.

playground.title: Playground
playground.author: Richard Powers
playground.why: A reader-praised novel by Powers set around the ocean and its people, enjoyed more as a story than as typical literary fiction.

cutting for stone.title: Cutting for Stone
cutting for stone.author: Abraham Verghese
cutting for stone.why: A multigenerational saga of twin brothers raised in an Ethiopian hospital, with medicine, family and a gripping story.

painted bird.title: The Painted Bird
painted bird.author: Jerzy N. Kosinski
painted bird.why: A harrowing wartime tale of a boy wandering rural Eastern Europe, remembered as nightmarish and unforgettable.

white noise.title: White Noise
white noise.author: Don DeLillo
white noise.why: A professor's family life and fear of death in consumer America, both absurdly funny and deeply unsettling.

bel canto.title: Bel Canto
bel canto.author: Ann Patchett
bel canto.why: A hostage drama set among opera lovers in a South American mansion; beautiful but slow-paced according to some readers.

less.title: Less
less.author: Andrew Sean Greer
less.why: A failing novelist travels the world to dodge his ex's wedding in a delightful comic novel that lifts reading slumps.

persuasion.title: Persuasion
persuasion.author: Jane Austen
persuasion.why: Austen's quiet second-chance love story, often named her best for its mature heroine and gentle feeling.

lonely hunter.title: The Heart is a Lonely Hunter
lonely hunter.author: Carson McCullers
lonely hunter.why: Lonely people in a small Southern town in the 1930s, bound by a deaf-mute man; a classic of Southern gothic.

little prince.title: the little prince
little prince.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
little prince.why: A short philosophical fable for adults and children about love, loneliness and what matters.

radium girls.title: The radium girls
radium girls.author: Kate Moore
radium girls.why: The true story of young women poisoned by radium paint in factories and their fight for justice.

earth abides.title: Earth abides
earth abides.author: George Rippey Stewart
earth abides.why: A survivor watches civilisation fall and slowly rebuild after a plague, a quiet pioneering post-apocalyptic novel.

light from uncommon stars.title: Light From Uncommon Stars
light from uncommon stars.author: Ryka Aoki
light from uncommon stars.why: A queer, genre-blending story of a violin teacher, a donut-shop owner and a space-faring secret, praised as unexpected.

sula.title: Sula
sula.author: Toni Morrison
sula.why: Two Black women's friendship and its breaking in a small Ohio town, short and heartbreaking.

absalom absalom.title: Absalom, Absalom!
absalom absalom.author: William Faulkner
absalom absalom.why: A broken Southern family saga told in dense, tangled prose; admired as Faulkner's masterwork but demanding.

blind assassin.title: The Blind Assassin
blind assassin.author: Margaret Atwood
blind assassin.why: A nested story of sisters, a scandal and a pulp novel within the novel, with a long slow-burning twist.

spin.title: Spin
spin.author: Robert Charles Wilson
spin.why: The stars vanish from the sky and time on Earth speeds up; big ideas wrapped around human characters.

mother night.title: Mother Night
mother night.author: Kurt Vonnegut
mother night.why: An American double agent in World War II and the moral cost of pretending; short and powerful Vonnegut.

wee free men.title: The Wee Free Men
wee free men.author: Terry Pratchett
wee free men.why: A young witch fights a fairy queen with the help of tiny blue men; a funny, warm Discworld entry for young readers.

under the banner of heaven.title: Under the Banner of Heaven
under the banner of heaven.author: Jon Krakauer
under the banner of heaven.why: An investigation of fundamentalist Mormon violence that also examines faith, favoured by readers who like gripping true crime.

dark tower.title: The Dark Tower
dark tower.author: Stephen King
dark tower.why: The final book of King's gunslinger epic, recommended by fans of the whole series as his big life's work.

gone with the wind.title: Gone With the Wind
gone with the wind.author: Margaret Mitchell
gone with the wind.why: A sweeping Civil War romance centred on Scarlett O'Hara, long and compelling though its views are controversial.

yellow wallpaper.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
yellow wallpaper.author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
yellow wallpaper.why: A short story of a woman losing her mind under confinement, widely read for its portrait of how women were treated.

bad blood.title: Bad Blood
bad blood.author: John Carreyrou
bad blood.why: The astonishing story of the Theranos fraud, told as a gripping page-turner that works well as an audiobook.

song of solomon.title: Song of Solomon
song of solomon.author: Toni Morrison
song of solomon.why: A Black man's search for his family's past and himself, favoured by readers as their top Morrison.

color purple.title: The Color Purple
color purple.author: Alice Walker
color purple.why: Letters and life of a Black woman in the American South; moving and widely read, with strong praise.

legend.title: I Am Legend
legend.author: Richard Matheson
legend.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

small gods.title: Small Gods
small gods.author: Terry Pratchett
small gods.why: A god stuck as a tortoise and a novice questioning the Church; one of the funniest and sharpest Discworld books.

thursday murder club.title: The Thursday Murder Club
thursday murder club.author: Richard Osman
thursday murder club.why: Four retirees solve cold cases in a care home; cosy, character-driven and easy, though not to every taste.

island.title: Island
island.author: Aldous Huxley
island.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

revelation space.title: Revelation Space
revelation space.author: Alastair Reynolds
revelation space.why: Space opera with deep time, ancient horrors and grim crews; hard sci-fi fans re-read the whole series.

last house on needless street.title: The Last House on Needless Street
last house on needless street.author: Catriona Ward
last house on needless street.why: A strange, twisty horror-thriller about a reclusive man and the haunted house he lives in.

warmth of other suns.title: The Warmth of Other Suns
warmth of other suns.author: Isabel Wilkerson
warmth of other suns.why: The story of the Great Migration of Black Americans from the South, told through three people's lives.

housemaid.title: The Housemaid
housemaid.author: Freida McFadden
housemaid.why: A domestic thriller about a maid in a wealthy home, a fast hook even for readers who dislike its style.

life after life.title: Life After Life
life after life.author: Kate Atkinson
life after life.why: A woman lives the same life again and again across the first half of the 20th century; some wept at the end.

lessons in chemistry.title: Lessons in Chemistry
lessons in chemistry.author: Bonnie Garmus
lessons in chemistry.why: A woman scientist in the 1960s is pushed into a cooking show; light, funny and warm.

starship troopers.title: Starship Troopers
starship troopers.author: Robert A. Heinlein
starship troopers.why: A soldier's training and war against alien bugs; a classic of military sci-fi and a source of many arguments.

roadside picnic.title: Roadside Picnic
roadside picnic.author: Arkady and Boris Strugatsky
roadside picnic.why: Stalkers sneak into a zone left by alien visitors to find artefacts; moving, strange and short.

once and future king.title: The Once and Future King
once and future king.author: T. H. White
